newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turk security council restates anti-Islamist aim.
newsitem.headline: Turk security council restates anti-Islamist aim.

text.p: Turkey's political and military leaders reaffirmed their aim to counter Islamist activism on Friday at the first National Security Council meeting since the new secularist government took office.

"All council members reached unanimity on the necessity to apply decisively measures...against fundamentalist activities harming the regime," a statement from the council secretariat was quoted as saying by Anatolian news agency.
The NSC demanded in February that the then Islamist-led government stem an alleged rise in the profile of religious activists, which it saw as a threat to the secular state.
Senior government ministers and military chiefs sat face-to-face in an Istanbul army base on Friday afternoon for a three-hour meeting chaired by President Suleyman Demirel.
Earlier they laid a wreath at the city's main monument to Turkey's secularist founder Kemal Ataturk.
The council decided to present the new cabinet with a report highlighting the failings of charitable foundations, many of which are Islamist in character.
The secularist pressure exerted by the council contributed to the collapse of the former coalition under Islamist Necmettin Erbakan.
After months of wrangling with the military and the country's secularist elite, Erbakan resigned last month, opening the way for a loose right-left alliance under Prime Minister Mesut Yilmaz.
At Friday's meeting the council stressed the importance of programmes to counter the negative impact of the armed conflict between the military and Kurdish rebels in southeastern Turkey.
More than 26,000 people have died since 1984 in the fight with the Kurdistan Workers Party (PKK) guerrillas, who seek self rule in the southeast of the country.
The council also addressed the problem of the divided island of Cyprus and developments in Turkey's relationship with the European Union, the statement said.
